lines: You ran the top like the bottom. Up there your feet take their time, and you have to let them.
You got up. Every Hare has, the first time on somebody's hip.
Good. You felt the stair go slow under you and went slow with it.
Light at the top and not one stumble. Are you sure nobody in your family is Hare?
The water was late, so the drum was slow. Send it before the train goes, not when you see it leave.
Sorrel turned a little slow this morning. Nobody will notice but me, and I'll mention it.
Trim enough. The gauge barely moved, and I was watching it.
A hundred and ten seconds a turn, all morning. The water knew where everyone went, and so did you.
Cold soup under other people's lids. Sit down, have a bowl, and look at the wall while you eat.
Most of them got their own lid, and warm enough. The rest were polite about it.
Hot, and under the right lids. A year of that and you'd earn a hook.
You know my wall better than I do, and I hung it. Lids on.
You brushed each tree onto itself. Nothing will come of it but the exercise.
Some will set. The crew will know which rows were yours by the apples that never come.
A good morning's brushing. I've put you on the rota for next week, and the week after.
Every blossom got its brush. I'd put you on every rota we have, and we have a rota for that.
You went home with what you came with. That isn't a both, that's a walk.
You got there the long way round. Half the market has had your things through its hands.
Nicely done. Everyone you swapped with thinks they won, which is the whole trick.
Straight there and not a swap wasted. I'd say sit down, but you'd price the chair.
Half a g gives you time to fix a bad dive. You spent it shouting.
You went in, mostly head first. The bench has seen worse, and said so.
Clean enough that your robe stayed dry on the rail. The elders gave you a nod.
No splash to speak of. The bench had its cards up before you surfaced.
It came down before the door shut. We'll stack it again, and this time you can watch.
It rode up, most of it. The rest is on the landing, being argued about.
A good stack. Heavy at the bottom and steady at the top, like a proper dinner.
Right to the top and not a wobble. That's heavy. You've earned your pudding.
You're wearing the tea. The gimbal does this ninety million times an hour and nobody thanks it.
Half a cup left. In a real cab you'd never have felt the lean, which is the point of us.
Most of the tea and the whole bun. You can ride with me.
Not a drop, through the brake and all. Leave early, arrive leaning.
A good chair in the steel bin. I've seen that done once before, and we still talk about him.
Sorted, more or less. I'll go through the bins after you. I go through them after everyone.
Tidy. Nothing went in a bin that had a year left in it.
Every scrap where it belongs, and the crusts in a pan. You may come again. Bring a jar.

host.name: Mahsa Ferro
host.role: remakes wing-sleeves, flew for sixty years

lines: You aimed at every hoop and the drum moved you off it. Aim where the turn is taking you.
A few lamps threaded. The warden only had to fetch you the once.
You let the turn carry you and corrected late, like a flyer. I sewed those fins. Mind them.
Crosswise all the way and never off the lamps. I flew for sixty years and managed that in about forty of them.
You threw like someone in the old pictures. Here the ball has opinions.
A few went in. Spin sinks, anti floats. You'll be saying it in your sleep.
That's a wing's arm. The Pack sang for you, and we don't sing for visitors.
Both ends, near and far. Come and eat: six to a pot, and you're the sixth.
That one's still on its way down. The higher you cook, the longer it's up there and the further it lands.
Breakfast was served, and a little late by Lark's reckoning. So, late.
Golden both sides and caught where it came down. Early.
Not one dropped, all the way up the wall. Early, early, early.
